note: Recast from Rocha & Cancello (2009), original in English; the original uses “ocellar spot” rather than the “eye spot” of Snyder (1923), the position being comparable to the ocellus of the alate; no measurement data.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is distinguished from the other species of the genus by the combination of large compound eyes and a fontanelle of medium size; the most similar species is O. aduncus, from which it differs in the ocelli touching the compound eye in lateral view. The soldier differs from all other species of the genus in the visible ocellar spot on the head capsule.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes large, separated from the lower margin of the head by less than the greatest diameter of an ocellus. Ocelli semicircular in dorsal view; oval in lateral view, separated from the compound eye by less than its least diameter. Fontanelle wide, of medium size. Head capsule with a few short hairs, fewer ventrally, setae present only on the dorsum. Labral setae not arranged in rows. Pronotum fairly densely covered with setae and short hairs; mesonotum and metanotum with short hairs, concentrated on the centre and the margins. Head dark brown, pronotum pale brown, tergites brown to pale brown, sternites yellow, legs and wing scales pale brown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head parallel in dorsal view. Dorsal tubercle prominent in lateral view, situated behind the lateral projection. Mandibles type 1, with a tooth-like process on the proximal half. A visible ocellar spot on the head capsule. Head capsule with short hairs and sparse setae, denser ventrally, minute hairs sparsely scattered over the whole head capsule. Postmentum with setae and short hairs. Surface of the pronotum with short hairs and setae, denser on the margins; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with setae; abdominal tergites densely covered with short hairs and setae, the sternites with short hairs and setae on the posterior margin.
